_whereToGetKeys.discordBotToken_clientId_clientSecret: https://discord.com/developers/applications — Discord Developer Portal: create an application, copy the Bot Token (Bot tab) and the Client ID + Client Secret (OAuth2 tab).
_whereToGetKeys.twitchClientId_clientSecret: https://dev.twitch.tv/console — Twitch Developer Console: register an application, copy the Client ID and Client Secret.
_whereToGetKeys.youtubeApiKey: https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/youtube.googleapis.com — Google Cloud Console: enable the YouTube Data API v3, then create an API key under APIs & Services > Credentials.
_whereToGetKeys.steamApiKey: https://steamcommunity.com/dev/apikey — Steam: sign in and register for a Web API key.
_whereToGetKeys.openAiApiKey: https://platform.openai.com/api-keys — OpenAI: create an API key. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works — set ai.baseUrl to use another provider.

dashboard._getItHere: https://discord.com/developers/applications — same Discord application: OAuth2 tab for the Client Secret; the redirect URI must match dashboard.redirectUri.

health._note: Localhost-only health endpoint the bot listens on (127.0.0.1) so the dashboard status page can tell whether the bot is online. Never exposed publicly; the dashboard fetches it server-side. Change the port here only if 3011 is taken.
